note: Suggested steps from common bookkeeping practice, not law or a regulator's checklist. Estimates are left blank for each firm to set. Edited by code review.

steps.title: Bank feeds are up to date for every account, card and payment platform (Stripe, PayPal, Square).
All supplier bills dated in the month are entered, including ones still in the inbox.
All sales invoices for work done in the month are raised.
Payroll for the month is posted, with super (AU) or pension and PAYE/NIC (UK) liabilities.
Every bank and card account reconciles to the statement closing balance.
Clearing and suspense accounts are at zero, or every item in them is explained.
Aged receivables and aged payables agree to the balance sheet control accounts.
The GST or VAT account agrees to the tax report for the period.
Payroll liabilities (PAYG, super, PAYE, pension) agree to the payroll reports.
Accrue expenses incurred but not yet billed (electricity, audit fees, contractor time).
Release one month of each prepayment (insurance, annual software) to expense.
Release deferred revenue earned this month; defer amounts billed in advance.
Post depreciation and amortisation from the fixed asset register.
Adjust inventory to the count or the perpetual records, and post write-downs to NRV.
Review old receivables; update the allowance for credit losses or write off what will not be paid.
Set last month's accruals to reverse on the first day of this month.
Read the trial balance: every balance on its normal side, nothing strange or unexplained.
Compare the P&L with last month and with budget; explain big swings.
Set the lock date in Xero or close the books in QBO.
Send the management pack (P&L, balance sheet, cash flow, aged reports).
Reconcile every bank and card account to the end of the period.
Review the GST coding of sales and purchases for the period and correct miscoded transactions.
Check that a tax invoice is held for each purchase where a GST credit is claimed.
Agree PAYG withholding on the BAS to the payroll reports.
Prepare the BAS from the GST report and compare it with the previous period.
Send the BAS to the client for review and approval.
Lodge the BAS and record the lodgment reference.
Tell the client the amount payable or refundable and when it is due.
Reconcile every bank and card account to the end of the VAT period.
Review the VAT codes on sales and purchases for the period and correct miscoded transactions.
Check that a VAT invoice is held for each purchase where input VAT is reclaimed.
Review reverse charge, postponed import VAT and partial exemption entries.
Prepare the VAT return from the VAT report and compare it with the previous period.
Send the VAT return to the client for review and approval.
Submit the return through MTD-compatible software and keep the submission receipt.
Tell the client the amount payable or repayable and when it is due.
Confirm the last month-end close of the year is complete and the period is locked.
Agree bank, loan and card balances to the year-end statements.
Agree receivables, payables and accruals to supporting schedules.
Update the fixed asset register and post the year's depreciation.
Count or confirm closing inventory and post the adjustment.
Post the year-end adjustments and prepare the final trial balance.
Prepare the financial statements and the tax computation.
Review the accounts and the tax return with the client and get sign-off.
File the accounts and lodge or submit the tax return.
Collect timesheets, leave and pay changes for the period.
Add new starters and process leavers.
Process the pay run and compare the payroll summary with the last run.
Approve the pay run with the client.
Pay employees and send payslips.
Report the pay run to the tax authority (Single Touch Payroll in Australia, RTI in the UK).
Post the payroll journal and the tax and super or pension liabilities.
